title: Projects
text:
Unsupervised Pangenomic Analysis of Paenibacillus polymyxa
CMPT 353 — Computational Data Science (Summer 2026)

GitHub Repository Project Report (PDF)


Developed an unsupervised machine learning pipeline in Python to analyze 62 P. polymyxa draft genomes, resolving species boundaries and evolutionary sub-lineages.
Engineered a custom GFF3 parsing module using Pandas to filter biological noise and extract Coding Sequences (CDS), constructing a \(62 \times 4,460\) binary presence/absence feature matrix.
Mapped global genomic variance via Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and evaluated population structures using K-Means and Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering (HCA) with Jaccard distance.
Extracted top genetic loading drivers across PC1 and PC2, and implemented targeted regex keyword profiling to compute a normalized Target Functional Index for pathogenic risk screening.

Key Technologies: Python, Pandas, Scikit-Learn, PCA, HCA, K-Means, Regular Expressions, Matplotlib.



Reliable Data Transfer Protocol over UDP
CMPT 371 — Data Communications and Networking (Fall 2025)

GitHub Repository Project Report (PDF)


Implemented a pipelined Reliable Data Transfer (RDT) transport protocol over UDP featuring cumulative ACKs and fast retransmit, achieving 100% in-order delivery across network conditions with packet loss, delay, duplication, and bit-error corruption.
Engineered TCP-style sliding window congestion control alongside receiver-advertised flow control to dynamically adapt cwnd and rwnd behavior during low-consume conditions.
Validated protocol invariants with a suite confirming handshake integrity, retransmission timeouts, and buffer allocation.

Key Technologies: Python, UDP Sockets, Network Simulation, Protocol Verification, Flow & Congestion Control.

title: Eric Cheung
text: I am a fourth-year computing science student at Simon Fraser University, combining a background in molecular biology and biochemistry. My coursework in machine learning, statistical learning, and computational biology has inspired a strong interest in how machine learning can be applied to genomic data and biological sequence modeling. I am particularly curious about exploring long-range sequence dependencies and computational tools in genomics. I aspire to bridge the gap between wet-lab biology and data-driven systems.

title: Research & Writing
text:
Benchmarking Long-Context Genomic Language Models for Synteny-Aware Antimicrobial Resistance Prediction
NSERC CGS-M Research Proposal (2026)

Open Proposal (PDF) Download

Overview:
Standard homology tools (e.g., BLAST, HMMER) evaluate resistance genes in isolation, frequently missing regulatory syntenic context and producing pseudogene false positives. This research proposal outlines a benchmarking framework for sub-quadratic, reverse-complement (RC) equivariant genomic language models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus) scaled across 1–32 kb windows. The framework benchmarks single-nucleotide resolution sensitivity to promoter motifs and frameshifts while evaluating out-of-distribution generalizability across diverse GC-content bacterial genomes.

Implementing Secure Genome Language Models for National Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance
CMPT 376W — Professional Responsibility and Technical Writing (Summer 2026)

Open Paper (PDF) Download

Overview:
A persuasive technical paper prepared for the Public Health Agency of Canada (PHAC) examining structural false-negative blind spots in legacy sequence homology tools when identifying novel, divergent antimicrobial resistance genes (<40% identity). It proposes a dual-layer implementation framework: an air-gapped, federated deployment ensuring strict patient metagenomic privacy, paired with a Two-Tier Verification System (0.8 probability commit cutoff and AttnLRP explainability validation) to combine sensitive deep learning detection with clinical auditability.
